title: feat: Support running as fully non-root containers

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A decision needs to be taken

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I'd like to run homarr fully rootless inside the container by specifying the `user: 1234:1234` directive in the compose file. However, this isn't feasible because current `entrypoint.sh` chowns everything as the root user and then drop privileges via su-exec. The issue has been reported in #2154 and #2597.

To alleviate this, I've tried mounting an `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` that follows some practices of [nginx-unprivileged](https://github.com/nginx/docker-nginx-unprivileged) like writing temp files to `/tmp`. I've also tried copying the `/app` repo to `/tmp` as the unprivileged user, and run the `run.sh` from there which worked. Details are as follow:

<details>
<summary>/etc/nginx/nginx.conf</summary>

```conf
events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

# +++ err log and pid to /tmp
error_log  /tmp/error.log notice;
pid        /tmp/nginx.pid;

http {
    # +++ write temp files to /tmp
    proxy_temp_path /tmp/proxy_temp;
    client_body_temp_path /tmp/client_temp;
    fastcgi_temp_path /tmp/fastcgi_temp;
    uwsgi_temp_path /tmp/uwsgi_temp;
    scgi_temp_path /tmp/scgi_temp;

    server {
        listen 7575;

        # Route websockets traffic to port 3001
        # +++ hardcode hostnames
        location /websockets {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3001;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection "Upgrade";
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
        }

        # Route all other traffic to port 3000
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://homarr:3000;
            proxy_set_header Host $http_host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $http_x_forwarded_proto;
            client_max_body_size 32M;
        }
    }
}

```

</details>

<details>
<summary>entrypoint.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
echo "Starting with UID='$PUID', GID='$PGID'"

cp -r /app /tmp
sh /tmp/app/run.sh
```
</details>


<details>
<summary>run.sh</summary>

```sh
# In line 4, add this command 
mkdir -p /tmp/logs

# ... other stuff ...

# add "-p /tmp" to the nginx command on line 26 or 27
# this will redirect logs to /tmp/logs/ as created above
nginx -g 'daemon off;' -p /tmp &
```

</details>

With this set up, I was able to spin up Homarr without using a root user on Podman, using this `podman-compose.yml` file:

```yaml
networks:
  test-network:
    external: true


services:
  homarr:
    container_name: homarr
    hostname: homarr
    image: ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - test-network

    # alternative entrypoint
    entrypoint: "/bin/sh"
    command: ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
    ports:
      - '7575:7575'

    # mount the aforementioned volumes into /app
    volumes:
      - ./homarr/appdata:/appdata
      - ./homarr/entrypoint.sh:/app/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/run.sh:/app/run.sh:ro
      - ./homarr/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
    env_file:
       - ./homarr.env    

    # security options
    user: 1234:1234
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      no-new-privileges: true
```

Insofar, I've been able to connect to my reverse proxy and set up OpenID Connect, and create a dashboard that persists on reboot. So I think it works. The only error log I see from this approach is that some cache actions are still expecting the original path, but I don't think it has a breaking effect overall

```
 ⨯ Failed to write image to cache LHuqnU3UxZpbO5f-Ux2znSfOhD2tmibMIt8ytqnjPAs [Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'] {
  errno: -13,
  code: 'EACCES',
  syscall: 'mkdir',
  path: '/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'
}
```

---

As this proof-of-concept seems feasible, I'd like to kindly request rootless, unprivileged container to be supported. The app and itself is already runnable as non-root, the only difference is that instead of chowning its path, I'm copy-pasting it to some other place. The demo should show that this hackaround (or any other alternative way to implement rootless) shouldn't be too difficult to implement, given it's just switching around a few stuff from the entrypoints.

Would this be a viable option to run Homarr? I hope there can be a full solution which helps increase the security of my containers. Thanks in advance

### Additional information

Disclaimer: I'm not a professional, just a hobbyist, proceed with above approach at your own risk

full_comments.body: Hm interesting, not sure if this will actually work in all use cases, but it's definitely something we can take a look at some point. Thanks for sharing your concept

This path (`'/app/apps/nextjs/.next/cache'`) can be probably se precreated on the dockerfile + be world writable so any whatever the user is starting the container, will be able to write.

Alternatively, I think you can configure the cache path via the next config so it lands in the appdata dir, which should be already writable, and cache will persist as well.

Regarding the docker integration, it can still run rootless, but the user will have to pass the docker group (along with the docker.sock) via group_add
ie `group_add: ["999"]` (where 999 is the docker group, it is probably different for each system)
